annotations.title: File a bank line (preview, then confirm)

description: File one unfiled bank line. Give ONE of: account_code (e.g. bank charges, income, a loan), invoice allocations / customer_id (customer receipt — remainder goes on account), bill allocations / supplier_id or supplier_name (supplier payment), or on_account:true with a customer or supplier. TWO STEPS: the first call changes nothing and returns a preview of the journal it will post plus a confirm_token; call again with exactly the same arguments plus confirm_token (valid 10 minutes, single use) to post it. Always show the user the preview and get their OK first. Changes the user's real books — only after they have seen the preview and agreed. Needs the user's GetAccountED sign-in (they are asked to sign in the first time).

account_code.description: File straight to this account (chart of accounts code)

allocations.description: Which invoices (money in) or bills (money out) this pays, with optional amounts (part payments allowed). Omit amount to settle as much as is due, in order.

amount.description: Rand allocated to this invoice or bill

business_id.description: Accounting practices only: which client's books (an id from accounting_list_my_businesses). Leave out to use the books chosen at sign-in.

confirm_token.description: Second step only: the token from the preview

customer_id.description: Customer id (inv client) — for a receipt; anything not allocated goes on account

on_account.description: Whole amount on account with the customer / supplier

refund.description: With account_code: money in that is a refund of an expense

supplier_id.description: Supplier contact id — for a supplier payment

supplier_name.description: Supplier known only by name on its bills

vat.description: With account_code: split 15% VAT out of the amount (VAT vendors only). Omit to use the default for that account.

name: accounting_file_bank_line
